# Runs the pipeline once a day, stores the output on the orphan `data` branch
# (latest/ + history/YYYY-MM-DD/), and calls pages.yml to redeploy the page when
# the latest data changed.

name: Daily pipeline

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 5 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: daily-pipeline
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  pipeline:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    outputs:
      data_changed: ${{ steps.snapshot.outputs.data_changed }}
    env:
      PROVIDERS: opencode-go opencode-zen cursor copilot clinepass openrouter
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci

      - name: Configure git
        run: |
          git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config --global user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Check out data branch
        run: |
          if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin data >/dev/null; then
            git fetch origin data
            git worktree add -B data data-branch origin/data
          else
            git worktree add --orphan -b data data-branch
          fi

      # Lets refresh.ts keep the previous pricing file when a parser fails, and fetch.ts
      # keep the previous Artificial Analysis data when rate limited, so the run can
      # still complete instead of crashing on a missing file.
      - name: Seed previous pricing data
        run: |
          mkdir -p data
          for src in $PROVIDERS; do
            if [ -d "data-branch/latest/$src" ]; then cp -r "data-branch/latest/$src" data/; fi
          done
          if [ -d "data-branch/latest/artificial-analysis" ]; then
            cp -r "data-branch/latest/artificial-analysis" data/
          fi

      # A nonzero exit (parser mismatch or network failure) fails this step immediately,
      # so the commit/build/deploy steps below are skipped and the published page is
      # left unchanged. Pi parser repair is local-only and refuses to run in Actions
      # (CI/GITHUB_ACTIONS are set), so a broken parser here is fixed locally and committed.
      - name: Run pipeline
        env:
          AA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AA_API_KEY }}
        run: npm start

      - name: Commit model mapping
        run: |
          if git diff --quiet -- config/model-mapping.json; then
            echo "No mapping changes."
            exit 0
          fi
          git add config/model-mapping.json
          git commit -m "Update model mapping"
          git pull --rebase origin main
          git push origin HEAD:main

      - name: Commit data snapshot
        id: snapshot
        run: |
          day=$(date -u +%F)
          for dest in latest "history/$day"; do
            mkdir -p "data-branch/$dest"
            cp data/recommendations.json "data-branch/$dest/"
            for src in $PROVIDERS; do
              mkdir -p "data-branch/$dest/$src"
              cp "data/$src/models-pricing.json" "data-branch/$dest/$src/"
            done
            mkdir -p "data-branch/$dest/artificial-analysis"
            cp data/artificial-analysis/language-models.json "data-branch/$dest/artificial-analysis/"
          done
          cd data-branch
          git add -A
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "No data changes."
            exit 0
          fi
          # history/ gets a new dir every day; only a change under latest/ affects the page.
          if ! git diff --cached --quiet -- latest; then
            echo "data_changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          git commit -m "Data for $day"
          git push origin HEAD:data

  deploy:
    needs: pipeline
    if: needs.pipeline.outputs.data_changed == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/pages.yml

content.text:
CI didn't fail, and the OpenRouter parser is working. The problem is in matching OpenRouter's model names to Artificial Analysis models. Only OpenRouter is affected: every other provider on the page has its 3 recommendations per category.

**What happened**
- The latest Daily pipeline run succeeded and wrote 461 OpenRouter models. It scored 93 models overall.
- OpenRouter names include a vendor prefix (`Google: Gemini 4 Carbon`, `Anthropic: Claude Fable 5.2`). AA names them without it (`Gemini 4 Carbon (High)`).
- `nameKey` in [update-mapping.ts](src/mapping/update-mapping.ts:18) only strips trailing `(…)` qualifiers, so the extra `google` word stops the names from matching. 351 of the 365 OpenRouter entries in [model-mapping.json](config/model-mapping.json) got `aaSlug: null` with "no Artificial Analysis match found".
- **Tencent Hy4 got through by coincidence.** AA calls it `Tencent Hy4`, so `Tencent: Hy4` produces the same words. Only 8 OpenRouter entries matched at all, and the rest of them are old models that drop out at scoring time. That leaves Hy4 as the only OpenRouter result on the page.

**The fix:** strip a leading `Vendor: ` before building the match key, and possibly try the unstripped name as a fallback. Entries whose `aaSlug` is null are re-matched on every run, so the next run would fill most of the 351 entries in automatically. No mapping edits would be needed by hand.

content.text:
OpenRouter now gets 3 recommendations per category instead of just Tencent Hy4. Typecheck, lint and format all pass.

**The change** is in [update-mapping.ts](src/mapping/update-mapping.ts): the matcher now strips a leading `Vendor: ` from the name before comparing it to Artificial Analysis names. If that finds nothing, it tries the full name, so `Tencent: Hy4` still maps to `tencent-hy4`. Names that already worked match the same way as before.

**What changed after running it on the local data:**
- 178 OpenRouter entries in [model-mapping.json](config/model-mapping.json) went from `null` to a real AA model, including Gemini 4 Carbon/Hydrogen, Claude Fable 5.2, Qwen4 Max and GPT-6.1. No other provider's entries changed.
- 218 models still have no match. Many of those are models AA doesn't benchmark at all.
- Scored models went from 93 to 137. OpenRouter's top picks now include Gemini 4 Carbon, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

I ran only the mapping and scoring steps on the data already on disk, not the full `npm start`, which downloads all the provider and AA data again. Once the updated mapping is pushed, the next daily run will use it and update the page.
